items.title: Preparation for Game 4
items.summary: To prepare for Game 4 (Saturday, October 3), I suggest that players definitely read the following items to refresh your…
items.content_html:
To prepare for Game 4 (Saturday, October 3), I suggest that players definitely read the following items to refresh your memories:

  • The summary of the objective drafting rules
  • The summary of the rules for resolving each branch point decision
  • The Political Favors action—I’m experimenting with the rule change that you can take this action any time you abstain (without needing to be almost out of drones)
  • The Adjust PPGP action (and the linked reminders of what PPGP is all about)
  • The summaries of each story card slot (or the single story card, if that’s all a slot has)
  • The list of players’ installations (really only to know that it’s there if you ever want to refer to it)

In addition, I will privately send each player the contents of the inside of their polity screen, so that they can remember what many of their polity goals are.

Beyond that, all of the following are (totally optional) suggestions for anybody who wants to further remind themselves about the game so far.

Suggestions for rules reminders:

  • The quick reference page (actions during branch points, drone recovery, installation placement)
  • The page of all action descriptions
  • The game concepts page (particularly bribes)

Suggestions for story and narrative so far:

  • The branch points and story cards we encountered in Game 3
  • The full text of all story cards
  • The in-character minutes of ISA meetings (each one has a summary, or read the whole thing if you want!)

Suggestions for reminders of the game setting:

  • The world of Cyclicity
  • Pronouns for AIs
  • Essential genes
  • Homo species

items.title: Wormhole Expeditions (action)
items.summary: As an action, any player may place as many drones from behind their screen as they wish onto the Wormhole…
items.content_html:
As an action, any player may place as many drones from behind their screen as they wish onto the Wormhole Expeditions card.

A player may remove as many of their drones as they like from that card when either the Interstellar Replication card or Interstellar Trade Goods card is drawn from the branch point deck. When they do so, they gain additional drones or supply ships as described on the drawn card.

When the solar cycle ends, all drones on the Wormhole Expeditions card are returned to their owners’ reserves.

items.title: Solar Flare Suppression (action)
items.summary: As an action, any player may place as many drones from behind their screen as they wish onto the Solar…
items.content_html:
As an action, any player may place as many drones from behind their screen as they wish onto the Solar Flare Suppression card.

When either of the following two cards are drawn:

  • Sunspot activity still intensifying
  • Sunspot activity still critical

If the number of face-up drones on the Solar Flare Suppression card equals or exceeds 6 times the number of marked boxes on that card:

  • Do not add the solar flare token.
  • Permanently replace the drawn sunspot activity card with the corresponding card without thesymbol.

items.title: Solar flares (game concept)
items.summary: Solar flare tokens can be brought into the game by a special card in the branch point deck, or by…
items.content_html:
Solar flare tokens can be brought into the game by a special card in the branch point deck, or by special sunspot cards. When they appear, they are placed on the Solar Flare Damage card. Multiple solar flares can bestow penalties on polities based on their unshielded installations (as described in the Shield Installation action).

  • When the Solar Flare Damage card has a 2nd solar flare token placed upon it: Each polity loses 1 supply ship for each of its unshielded Outer Zone installations.
  • When the Solar Flare Damage card has a 3rd solar flare token placed upon it:
    • Each polity loses 1 supply ship for each of its unshielded Middle Zone installations.
    • All unshielded Outer Zone installations are destroyed and removed from the game.

items.title: Solar Flare Mitigation (action)
items.summary: As an action, any player may place as many drones from behind their screen as they wish onto the Solar…
items.content_html: Once per game, if a solar flare token would be added to the Solar Flare Damage card, and the number of drones on the Solar Flare Mitigation card equals or exceeds the number of marked boxes on that card: do not add the solar flare token.

items.title: Shield Installations (action)
items.summary: Place up to 3 supply ships from the reserve underneath any combination of your Middle Zone and Outer Zone installations.
items.content_html:
Place up to 3 supply ships from the reserve underneath any combination of your Middle Zone and Outer Zone installations. These supply ships can shield installations (which is relevant to the Solar Flare Damage card).

  • An Outer Zone installation is considered shielded if it has at least 2 supply ships underneath it.
  • A Middle Zone installation is considered shielded if it has at least 1 supply ship underneath it.
  • (Inner Zone installations are always considered shielded.)

items.title: Second Stage Transition—Conclusion
items.summary: When all players have finished recording their allocations for the third round, turn all their third-round cards face up for…
items.content_html:
When all players have finished recording their allocations for the third round, turn all their third-round cards face up for everyone to see.

It’s recommended for players to pair up and quickly check the arithmetic of each other’s drone allocations. If a player has spent more supply ships than they had available, their drone allocations will be carried out as fully as possible starting from the top of the card.

Determining final control

Start by determining final control of the outpost with the most total drones on it. In the event of a tie, the player with the first-place ranking card chooses which outpost to address. Any players who allocated drones to this outpost simultaneously add their drones now (keeping them separate from the drones that were already there, so that it can still be determined how many drones were placed in the first pair of rounds). The two players with the most drones on the outpost at this point are now co-sponsors of that outpost.

  • Any ties are broken in favor of the player(s) in control of the outpost at the end of the second round, or (if needed) in favor of the player(s) who had more drones on the outpost at the end of the second round. If a tie persists, the player(s) in control of the outpost at the end of the second round decide(s) which of the tied players share(s) control of it.

When the two polities co-sponsoring this outpost have been determined, remove all of their drones from the other two outposts (and remove all other players’ drones from the first outpost). Then determine final control of the remaining outpost that has the most total drones on it, in the same way as the first outpost. The third outpost is automatically co-sponsored by the two polities who are not co-sponsors of either of the first two outposts.

Give each polity their Polity Outpost tiles. Next, determine the nature of each outpost’s co-sponsorship and put the correspondoing Central Outpost tile into play:

  • If neither co-sponsoring polity placed a drone on the Seize Authority card, give the pair of polities the Cooperative tile corresponding to their outpost.
  • If exactly one co-sponsoring polity placed a drone on the Seize Authority card, give the pair of polities the Authority Seized tile corresponding to their outpost.
  • If both co-sponsoring polities placed a drone on the Seize Authority card, give the pair of polities the Malfunctioning tile corresponding to their outpost.

All these Central Outpost tiles have rules on the back that describe how the Polity Outpost tiles are positioned and what their action spots do. In every game from now on, the two polities co-sponsoring each outpost must be seated next to each other.

Finally, determine control of all installations. Starting with the player with the 1st-place ranking card:

  • Any other players who allocated drones to installations on the 1st-place player’s mat add their drones to those installations now.
  • The 1st-place player then allocates drones to their own installations (only the ones with foreign drones on them are relevant). Final control is dictated by whoever has the most drones, with ties broken the same was as for stations.
  • Any installations on the 1st-place player’s mat that are controlled by other players are given to those players, keeping them separate from their installation mats for now.

The same procedure is then resolved for the 2nd-place player, and so on.

Restoring installation mats

Remove all installations from your installation mat, keeping track of which ones were on arcs 1, 2, and 3, and which ones came from outposts or other players. Flip your installation mat back to its main side. Place your installations on your mat as follows:

  • All installations from your 1 arc and 2 arc go into your Inner Zone. If there isn’t enough room in your Inner Zone, choose which extra installation(s) to put in your Middle Zone.
  • All installations from your 3 arc go into your Middle Zone. If there isn’t enough room in your Middle Zone, choose which extra installation(s) to put in your Outer Zone.
  • Any installations you stole from other players go into your Outer Zone. If there isn’t enough room in your Outer Zone, choose which extra installation(s) to remove from the game.

Remember that installations must always go as far to the left as possible in their zones, in any order you choose, and that the gravity rules are always in effect.

Congratulations—civilization has now entered its Interstellar Stage. Discard all Second Stage Transition cards, and either save the game for the next session or start the next game immediately!
